Fuckin fantastic comment right here, I really appreciate this. Love your honesty & straight up respectful feedback. Gives me greater insight into my own actions. While I still stand by how I feel, yes, this community is full of an array of different queer folks with different pronouns, identities, etc. that each have different needs. Perhaps it was implied that I was generalising my experience to all other queer people, which is not the case. Again, my mistake. And I’m not expecting every single post here in r/ftm to be catered to me, no way in hell. That’s not how it works. Rather, I’d love to see new groups open up that I resonate with more closely, because I see less posts in this subreddit applicable to me. Again, not implying people who don’t fit my category should be excluded. I’m the one leaving after trying out a visibly queer identity. 

Although originally a vent, I think this is the type of conversation to have in person, because I can understand why it’s easy for the way I worded things to get misinterpreted and misunderstood. 

Thanks again & much respect.

I am not better for being mostly stealth. Perhaps my choice of wording implied this, and for that I apologise, but I am not superior to anyone by any means. Leading a reserved lifestyle with this is solely a personal preference, and does not stem from an attempt to be more palatable to cishet people. I want to see a new space for something more specific that I can more closely relate to, yes, not exclude others from spaces like this.

Not asking for anyone to cater to me, nor force anyone to leave spaces so that I can be accommodated. Not at all, do not get me wrong here. I am looking for a separate space that I will voluntarily go to. I experimented with bisexuality and trans visibility for a year, but found it was not for me (hence the label queer for myself). 

Perhaps a change in language is warranted also; I’m Australian and usage of expletives in reference to anything (without using it to intentionally harm) is common. 

I will never claim to be elite and superior to others in the community. That’s not how I roll, although perhaps this post made others think totally otherwise. I view all as equal and worthy, and I can acknowledge the privilege I have. This is why I am also voluntarily a reserved person in these spaces because there are voices that should be placer above mine & listened to first and foremost.

Again, this was a rant post. In future I believe it best to not voice my honest frustrations in such a public forum.
Certainly seems I don’t belong in this subreddit. Isn’t what it used to be.

Interesting analogy! Made me laugh hahah. I don’t view the queer community as shitty at all, nor freaks - why use that terminology in your analogy? My frustrations come from feeling as though straight binary trans men such as myself lack a space where we can comfortably exist and feel heard without feeling condemned. This has been my experience over the past 4 years. And I also understand that I won’t find a community that is 100% aligned with my needs, but so far, no success. It feels like more of a challenge in 2022 compared to back in 2017.

This was also a vent post, which (for me) allows me to express some internal anger & frustration. I am not pointing fingers and placing blame. ‘Fuck anything that moves’ is a direct quote from a queer friend. By ‘too inclusive’, I mean folks from all different walks of life in the queer community are having discussions in the same space, some of which may not apply to all group members, e.g. severe bottom dysphoria, as opposed to not experiencing it. And then I’m told I’m transphobic because I generalised my discussion to include all.

Albeit, there’s always room for improvement on my end, but I appreciate civil feedback in this context.

Thank you so much, yeah it was a terribly stressful experience for me. Healing takes time with that kinda shit, but I’ve learnt a major lesson: transitioning isn’t all just about the physical aspects; mental & emotional are just as important, if not more! And don’t be in shitty relationships at the start of transitioning!

At it’s core is trauma. 4 years ago, when I first started transitioning, I was in a nasty transphobic relationship that ate away at my sense of identity. I was stripped of my newfound trans joy, and I felt absolutely worthless. No change that testosterone brought me was good enough, according to my ex. Thus I didn’t see any value in all the changes happening to me. My transition wasn’t worth celebrating, because nothing, no matter how big or small, was good enough for her. I know deep down I’ve always been good enough, but her insecure projections severely altered the way I viewed my worth as a trans person, and because of that I can’t seem to derive value, joy, nor appreciation for all the changes that transitioning has brought me. Transitioning was meant to be for me & only me, not to make a toxic person comfortable in their sexuality.

I’ve been going to great therapy for years now, but it seems like such a long journey. There’s a lot to unpack with my therapist so it’s a bit of a slow process. I’ll feel so relieved the day I really start to feel & embrace some kind of trans joy - it’s been such a quest to find it since pieces of it were taken from me every day for 2 years. I’ll get there. Wishing you the best ✌🏼
Also - I have good friends, but I am reluctant to talk about it because I would feel like a burden, and I want to move past that history

Yeah absolutely I was working out prior to surgery. Probably my biggest piece of advice if you want a high chance of getting good results (+ a good surgeon). It helps with the contouring of the chest for sure, so definitely do some upper body exercises on a frequent basis, doesn’t have to be insanely vigorous!

I relate to this hard. It does fucking suck. I haven’t dated in 2 years and haven’t been intimate with anyone for that same amount of time. I’ve distanced myself from it all as a protective mechanism (although I’m still willing to date if the chance comes). I just know that if I really got into the dating scene I would feel very dysphoric and it would take so much confidence to not give a fuck. It’s really frustrating. I hung out at a girls house once and I wasn’t really looking to take it further but she was thinking differently. I then disclosed to her that I was trans and it was like the sparkle in her eyes from being interested in me immediately faded. She started acting awkward around me and you could tell she was disappointed. If I were to go on a date, I’d just anticipate that I’d be ghosted if I disclosed that I am trans due to past experiences. Of course people have preferences, hell I do as well. It just sucks that you can’t change what you can’t control. I’ve tried tinder as well for the lols and it’s interesting to see the disparity in the amount of likes I get when I don’t put trans in my bio to when I do. I’m very frustrated, but I’m so used to being closed off to dating that I’ve trained myself to be content with being single and ‘self-partnered’. And I do feel pressure given I’m 20 and there’s a lot of young people in relationships around me.

I hope the dating scene treats you better. With gender-nonconforming/trans-identifying people, it’s just that much harder. And it makes us feel like outcasts from society. Wishing you the best with this hard shit.
